The following local comparison will prove both equality for analytic restrictions and additivity of the trace data. It reuses the divisorial error estimate from \cref{chap:hermitian-igood}.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:analytic-minorant-product-ideals}
Let $u,v$ be quasi-plurisubharmonic on a compact complex manifold, and let $s$ have analytic singularities. If $u+v\leq s+O(1)$, then for analytic potentials $U_m,V_m$ of types $(1/m,\mathcal I(mu))$, $(1/m,\mathcal I(mv))$, there are numbers $\delta_m\downarrow0$ such that
\[
 U_m+V_m\leq(1-\delta_m)s+O(1)
 \quad\hbox{for all sufficiently large integers }m.
\]
The bounded error may depend on $m$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Resolve the ideal of $s$ and write its singular part locally as
$\sum_i c_i\log|z_i|^2$, with $c_i>0$. Set
$A_i=1+\operatorname{ord}_{E_i}(\operatorname{Jac}\pi)$.
The hypothesis and \cref{lem:bergman-divisorial-error} give
\[
 \nu(U_m\circ\pi,E_i)+\nu(V_m\circ\pi,E_i)
 \geq\nu(u\circ\pi,E_i)+\nu(v\circ\pi,E_i)-\frac{2A_i}{m}
 \geq c_i-\frac{2A_i}{m}.
\]
Choose a positive integer $C\geq\max_i2A_i/c_i$ and put $\delta_m=C/m<1$ for large $m$. After a smooth local correction, divisorial removal from the positive Hessian of $(U_m+V_m)\circ\pi$ shows that
\[
 (U_m+V_m)\circ\pi-(1-\delta_m)\sum_i c_i\log|z_i|^2
\]
has a quasi-plurisubharmonic representative. It is locally bounded above. A finite resolution cover and proper descent therefore give
$U_m+V_m\leq(1-\delta_m)s+O(1)$, just as in \cref{lem:analytic-ideal-dominance}. The bounded constant may depend on $m$. If the divisor is empty, $s$ is bounded and upper bounds for $U_m,V_m$ prove the assertion directly.
\end{proof}

edits.old: By \cref{lem:divisorial-potential-domination} and \eqref{eq:curve-fiber-divisorial-current}, a quasi-plurisubharmonic $a$ is more singular than $v$ if and only if $\nu(a,Y_b)\geq\tau_{C,U}(b)$ for each positive coefficient. These fiber inequalities are among the defining trace constraints, and ordinary domination implies all the constraints on further modifications, by the exact formula just proved. Thus the full trace competitor family equals the ordinary-envelope family, and also the family defined by ideal domination. The envelope $Q_\Omega[v]$ was defined using ideal equivalence rather than domination, but this gives the same supremum: replace any member $a$ of the ordinary family by $\max\{a,v-\sup_Yv\}$. The replacement dominates $a$, remains below zero and is ordinarily, hence ideally, equivalent to $v$. Conversely every ideal-equivalent competitor belongs to the ideal-domination family. These comparisons prove the first two equalities in \eqref{eq:curve-fibration-trace-envelope}. The ideal envelope preserves the multiplier ideals and hence the fiber Lelong numbers; the lemma gives $Q_\Omega[v]\preceq v$. Since it dominates $v-\sup_Yv$, ordinary equivalence follows.

edits.old:
The addition inequality can be strengthened to equality. The needed approximation comparison is local; the global closed-current notation in which it was originally formulated is not a restriction on this application. We give the calculation in our weight convention. It is the resolution argument underlying Cao's addition theorem \cite{Cao15}.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:analytic-minorant-product-ideals}
Let $u,v$ be quasi-plurisubharmonic on a compact complex manifold, and let $s$ have analytic singularities. If $u+v\leq s+O(1)$, then for analytic potentials $U_m,V_m$ of types $(1/m,\mathcal I(mu))$, $(1/m,\mathcal I(mv))$, there are numbers $\delta_m\downarrow0$ such that
\[
 U_m+V_m\leq(1-\delta_m)s+O(1)
 \quad\hbox{for all sufficiently large integers }m.
\]
The bounded error may depend on $m$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Resolve the ideal of $s$. Locally upstairs,
\[
 s\circ\pi=\sum_i c_i\log|z_i|^2+O(1),\qquad c_i>0.
\]
The assumed inequality gives
$\nu(u\circ\pi,E_i)+\nu(v\circ\pi,E_i)\geq c_i$.
Choose nonnegative $a_i,b_i$ below these respective Lelong numbers with $a_i+b_i=c_i$. Local Siu decomposition, after smooth corrections, implies
\[
 u\circ\pi\leq\sum_i a_i\log|z_i|^2+O(1),\qquad
 v\circ\pi\leq\sum_i b_i\log|z_i|^2+O(1).
\]
Put $A_i=1+\operatorname{ord}_{E_i}\operatorname{Jac}\pi$. Pullback integrability of $f\in\mathcal I(mu)$ and $g\in\mathcal I(mv)$ gives
\[
 \operatorname{ord}_{E_i}(f\circ\pi)+A_i>ma_i,
 \quad \operatorname{ord}_{E_i}(g\circ\pi)+A_i>mb_i,
\]
and hence
\[
 \operatorname{ord}_{E_i}((fg)\circ\pi)>mc_i-2A_i.
\]
Choose $\delta_m=C/m$ with $C\geq\max_i2A_i/c_i$. Holomorphic division by the corresponding coordinate monomials, followed by logarithms of the finite generator norms, gives
\[
 (U_m+V_m)\circ\pi
 \leq(1-\delta_m)\sum_i c_i\log|z_i|^2+O(1).
\]
Proper descent and a finite cover prove the assertion. If the divisor is empty, $s$ is bounded and the conclusion follows from upper bounds for $U_m,V_m$. Smooth local corrections ensure positivity for Siu decomposition; no global closed background is used.
\end{proof}
edits.new: The addition inequality can be strengthened to equality. We apply the local approximation comparison \cref{lem:analytic-minorant-product-ideals}, the resolution argument underlying Cao's addition theorem \cite{Cao15}. No global closed background is needed.
